title: Why lay patent answers usually miss the claims
why: Most lay answers misread patent claims; real prosecution usually takes several rejections and RCEs, so a first rejection is no victory.

title: Solo founder's break-even timeline anecdote
why: Personal story of reaching break-even; no transferable technical or business lesson beyond one founder's experience.

title: Reflections on nerds and pop culture
why: Personal musings on staying culturally relevant and aging; opinion without technical substance.

title: Defense of a past Facebook partner integration
why: Anecdote defending a past partnership against press coverage; asserts innocence without explaining the technical facts.

title: Why Secure Boot cert extraction sparked a kernel fight
why: Redhat's patch extracted x.509 certs from Microsoft-signed UEFI binaries so Linux could verify signed modules; Linus rejected it.

title: Users tolerate bad software that solves problems
why: Opinion that quality matters only in saturated markets; asserted without evidence or analysis.

title: Why type erasure helped the JVM host languages
why: Erasure avoids crippling the runtime for other languages; specialization can come from compilers without reification, as Scala's @specialize shows.

title: Political complaint about US treatment of visitors
why: Political argument about tourist and worker treatment with personal grievance; no technical or factual lesson.

title: Quitting jobs over unfair treatment
why: Personal career anecdote about underpayment and quitting; no transferable lesson beyond general grievance.

title: Reflections on growing up with the internet
why: Personal nostalgia essay about the old internet and aging; no informational content.

title: How surprise billing laws shift negotiating power
why: Out-of-network threat gives physicians bargaining leverage; banning surprise billing removes that leverage, favoring insurers' rate pressure.

title: Finding book mentions with fine-tuned BERT
why: Name matching fails on ambiguous titles; a BERT model fine-tuned on labeled comments tags book mentions in context.

title: Childhood struggles with autism and bullying
why: Personal account of diagnosis and bullying; moving but without a transferable lesson beyond individual experience.

title: Argument that overhead keeps products stable
why: Opinion that large-company overhead provides stability; general claims about decay with no concrete evidence.

title: Where C# falls short for low-level code
why: C# lacks inline fixed arrays and value-type array access, and its stdlib invalidation checks make many operations linear.

title: Why minimal frameworks feel close to the metal
why: Author's preference for minimal frameworks and shared JS; a code sample but mostly opinion about developer preferences.

title: Critique of a jobs-and-gender article
why: Argues about article framing and gender claims; debate rather than explanation of anything technical.

title: Tax logic behind Australian investment property
why: Investment-property mortgage interest is deductible while home interest isn't; capital gains tax applies only on sale, so holders often never sell.

title: Anecdote and claims about birth control drugs
why: Mixes pharmacology facts with a questionable claim that Beyaz isn't antiandrogenic, plus anecdote; not reliable enough to keep.

title: Why car-dependent suburbs persist in hot cities
why: Opinion on walkability in hot cities plus cul-de-sac preference; sensible points but mostly argument with no data.

title: The Now Habit's unschedule and 30-minute chunks
why: Schedule fixed commitments first, then fill free time; commit to 30-minute work chunks and credit only uninterrupted productive time.

title: How type ratings constrained the 737 MAX fix
why: Argues Boeing skipped sensor-disagreement logic to protect the 737 common type rating, since disabling MCAS would have required new pilot training.

title: Opinion on engagement-maximizing product design
why: Complaints about Messenger and YouTube recommendations; personal preference rather than analysis.

title: Opinion on 10x developers and code decay
why: Argues good developers keep codebases from degrading; reasonable but opinion-driven with a few anecdotes.

title: Layered essay writing tool pitch
why: Product pitch for a layered essay tool with mockups; a project announcement rather than teaching.

title: Critique of an article on cloud pricing
why: Rebuts a Google-favoring article; notes sustained-use discounts complicate billing, but mostly argues against the piece.

title: Political argument about centralization and trust
why: Political argument about decentralized power and US media; opinion and rhetoric without technical content.

title: Opinion on Berlin housing and urban demand
why: Urban housing opinion generalizing about residents rather than explaining mechanisms with evidence.

title: Personal advice on health and social life
why: Personal life-reset story with general advice; useful to some but not a technical or insight-rich lesson.

title: Why array languages favor expressivity over abstraction
why: Array languages like J favor expressivity by avoiding premature abstraction, so codebases stay smaller and easier to read.

title: Opinion favoring explicit function constraints
why: Argues for typed function constraints over colorless functions; a stance on language design without new mechanism or evidence.

title: Mathematicians' critiques of US math teaching
why: Lists papers by Wu, Askey, Howe, Kenschaft and Milgram critiquing US K-12 math, with comparisons to practice in other countries.

title: Why ML overfits noisy financial data
why: Financial signals have R-squared near 1%, so complex models overfit; linear regression or latent-parameter models usually beat flexible ML.

title: Polemic against banks and finance pay
why: Polemic claiming banks create money from nothing and carry no risk; loose claims and rhetoric rather than verified analysis.

title: Why systemd beats shell-script init systems
why: Shell-based init spawns many processes per service; systemd forks and waits on services and gets kernel notice of crashes, avoiding polling.

title: Early-adopter review of Dell XPS 13 for Linux
why: First-hand review of keyboard and battery; useful for buyers but personal impressions rather than a transferable technical lesson.

title: Complaint about unacknowledged prior work
why: Critiques blog posts that reinvent projects without citing prior art; a meta-complaint without new technical content.

title: Personal complaints about Zipcar service
why: Anecdotes about Zipcar availability and car condition; consumer complaint with no general lesson beyond one experience.

title: Why GNOME 3 and Unity chased touch-first design
why: Desktop teams pursued touch-friendly redesigns after the iPhone's success and mobile funding, not mainly Microsoft threats, per this account.

title: Opinion that NFTs suit gaming
why: Speculative take on NFT gaming and gambling with no concrete mechanism; mainly enthusiasm rather than informative analysis.

title: Technology spun off from particle physics
why: Collider programs produced the web, LHC superconducting magnets, radiation-hard ASICs, and petabyte-scale distributed data pipelines as byproducts.

title: Opinion on US fighter procurement
why: Political and strategic opinion about F-35 and F-22 numbers and budgets; contentious claims without sourced analysis.

title: Rebuttal to Node.js criticism
why: Defends Node against hyperbole and praises Babel; rhetorical response with little concrete technical explanation.

title: Designing a house to cool without AC
why: Cross-ventilation, high ceilings, and an attic window create stack effect that pulls hot air up and out, so open windows at night flush heat.

title: Why ARM64 decodes faster and orders memory weaker
why: x86 variable-length instructions force decoding at every byte offset; fixed-width A64 decodes trivially but needs software fences for strict ordering.

title: Buffer hiring post with company metrics
why: Job advertisement with company metrics and roles; promotional rather than explanatory.

title: Why iCloud sync struggles with conflicts
why: A dumb file-sync server gives no canonical state, so clients must resolve conflicts from diffs, making consistent Core Data reconstruction very hard.

title: Libertarian vs socialist framing of software
why: Political argument using the non-aggression principle to judge licenses and company actions; ideological rather than technical.

title: Argument about MIT and immigration revenue
why: Political and economic argument about university revenue and immigration; opinion rather than evidence or mechanism.

title: Why Shenzhen's advantage isn't just cheap labor
why: Talent and infrastructure drive Shenzhen's manufacturing edge; the hukou system ties people to birthplace, shaping who can compete locally.

title: Why hospital IT lags so far behind
why: Hospitals rely on custom legacy EMRs, fax, and vendor lock-in; small markets and heavy customization make modern security retrofits very hard.

title: Why IPv6 adoption is slow: supply and demand
why: Address scarcity could be relieved by a liquid market for blocks, since most users never need public addresses and tunneling reduces pressure.

title: Which formal methods engineers actually use
why: Engineers reason about programs with TLA+, SPIN, B-Method, or Alloy since Coq is much harder; simple state-machine math covers most needs.

title: Opinion that Rust is a poor general-purpose language
why: Argues Rust exposes low-level detail and suits only performance-sensitive work; a stance rather than a measurement.

title: Why 64-bit pointers suffice and what CHERI adds
why: 64-bit addresses cover 16 EiB; CHERI pointers carry bounds and permissions in 128 bits, while C's long-as-pointer assumption hampers portability.

title: Why batteries can't cover renewable grid storage
why: At 12 hours of storage, global needs reach about 35,000 GWh, roughly 70 years of current battery output, so scale is badly mismatched.

title: Sysadmin hiring post for a hosting company
why: Job advertisement for an entry-level sysadmin with pay and arrangement details; promotional rather than instructive.

title: Developers fund App Store refunds, Apple keeps commission
why: Per Apple's developer agreement, developers reimburse refunds Apple issues, and Apple keeps its commission on refunded sales.

title: Rant against a Google diversity memo
why: Moral argument condemning a memo and defending diversity programs; political discourse without technical content.

title: Running a fully remote company at GitLab
why: Remote-first hires outside expensive metros and cuts office costs; the CEO notes that remote-first and remote-friendly are unsettled terms.

title: Law of Demeter and the book object example
why: Exposing nested internals like chapters to sections ties callers to structure; Demeter's rule limits navigation through intermediaries so restructuring stays safe.

title: Events and jobs need different messaging models
why: Events fan out to every subscriber type, while jobs go to exactly one processor with completion tracking; RabbitMQ fits events better than jobs.

title: Passive SaaS income through referrals and maintenance
why: Mid-five-figure MRR with about 30 minutes of daily support and referral-driven growth; a concrete case of low-maintenance subscription income.

title: Essay on apocalyptic mood and short-term greed
why: Broad cultural essay about apocalyptic mood and global warming; speculative sociology without evidence.

title: Question about the appeal of cruises
why: Asks why people enjoy cruises, with complaints about the experience; a question with no informative answer in the thread.

title: Opinion against saving dying languages
why: Contrarian opinion that language loss is efficient; a value judgment without evidence, though it touches linguistic diversity debates.

title: Personal reasons for leaving the tech industry
why: Personal career story about tedium and colleagues; resonant but an individual account rather than a transferable lesson.

title: Publishing industry censorship anecdote
why: Political anecdote about a literary agency and cancellation; a contested social story rather than technical content.

title: Why metadata falls under the third-party doctrine
why: Records generated and held by carriers fall under the third-party doctrine, so arguing metadata is your data faces an uphill legal battle.

title: California zoning blocks shared small-home communities
why: Most California counties allow one large single-family home per parcel, so shared tiny-home clusters need variances, making projects politically fragile.

title: Monads explained via functors and map
why: Explains functors as containers with map that can change element type, the basis for teaching monads through code instead of category theory.

title: Pitch for a startup toolkit
why: Lists startup components and pitches a product to build them; promotional rather than explanatory.

title: Opinion that Web3 is driven by speculation
why: Argues Bitcoin's price drives Web3 hype and scams; cynical opinion without technical analysis.

title: Author defends client-side rendering choice
why: Defends a personal site's JS rendering and dependency choices; reasonable tradeoffs but mostly a justification of one site.

title: Argument about gender in CS hiring
why: Argues early bias explains the tech gender gap and that hiring targets lower the bar; contentious argument with an analogy and no data.

title: Opinion on locked-down computing platforms
why: Argues users are losing control of hardware and OS choice; a stance that cites Doctorow but offers no new mechanism.

title: Niche sites that actually test products
why: Domain-specific sites like OutdoorGearLab, DCRainMaker, and SoundOnSound give more trustworthy reviews than SEO affiliate lists dominating Google results.

title: Questions on the endgame of sanctions
why: Asks what sanctions aim for and whether trade isolation backfires; open political questions rather than informative analysis.

title: Finding community when lonely online
why: Joining topic-based discussions beats signaling desperation, which attracts predators more than friends; support groups often unhelpful.

title: Short selling is legal; manipulation isn't
why: Per the SEC guidance cited, shorting is legal, but schemes to manipulate prices or engineer short squeezes are illegal.

title: Attack on Sci-Hub founder's politics
why: Political attack on the person behind Sci-Hub using translated quotes; not about the technical or legal merits.

title: Opinion on SNCF reform
why: Argues SNCF needs cost cuts and less political control; policy opinion with little supporting analysis.

title: Defense of dropping www in URLs
why: Argues usability beats technical purism in dropping www; a pro-simplification opinion without evidence.

title: Opinion on platform moderation and free speech
why: Argues private platforms acting as public squares is dangerous; policy opinion without a concrete mechanism.

title: Hiring signals beyond technical skill
why: Lists practical interview signals like adaptability, openness, desire to ship, and rationality; a concrete heuristic set, though subjective.

title: Critique of an overhyped developmental biology claim
why: Mostly meta-commentary on journalistic overclaiming and probability maxims; little concrete explanation of the underlying biology.

title: Requirements for a sync clipboard manager
why: Lists design goals for a cross-platform clipboard with sync and deletion; a requirements list without explained mechanisms.

title: Anecdote on Toronto house buying
why: Personal homebuying experience and complaints about bidding tactics; anecdotal opinion with limited general lesson.

title: Essay on victimhood as identity
why: Cultural opinion about victimhood and bias; personal reflection without evidence or technical content.

title: Argument about drug war and family structure
why: Political argument linking incarceration and family structure with statistics but a contested causal story.

title: Pitch for a Linux VR headset
why: Project pitch for a Linux VR headset with specs and window management; promotional rather than explanatory.

title: Income-based repayment's household-income blind spot
why: Federal income-based repayment ignores spousal income, and filing separately changes tax brackets; the comment shows a 30-year 6% loan repays about 216% of principal.

title: Opinion on an Airbnb damage incident
why: Argues about liability and a host's reaction, speculating on motives without facts; opinion about an ongoing story.

title: Personal gadget kit for daily carry
why: Personal list of gadgets carried daily with adapter specifics; a personal inventory rather than a general lesson.

title: Argument on photography and flight security
why: Opinion on airline security judgments and a statement made to crew; rhetorical rather than informative about policy.

title: Training Spotify recommendations with seed playlists
why: Seed a mood playlist with about ten songs, play its recommendations, add keepers, and prune stale tracks to steer the algorithm over time.

title: How federal sentences are actually calculated
why: Statutory maximums rarely apply; the mostly-mandatory Guidelines set a range from offense level and adjustments, so first offenders usually serve far less.

title: Argument on short-term rentals and neighbors
why: Argues short-term renters harm owner-occupied buildings and neighbors; mostly rhetorical, with a passing owner-occupier heuristic.

title: Opinion on why stocks rise in bad economies
why: Argues there is no alternative to stocks and that wealth concentration explains prices; partly sensible framing but mostly opinion.

title: Verify Bitcoin issuance yourself with gettxoutsetinfo
why: Any node can run gettxoutsetinfo to check total bitcoin issued without trusting anyone; the monetary policy is enforced in validation code.
